subject: understanding 2PL parameterization with pre-specified latent variable scale

messages.author: 1c0ff2f277b730d0
messages.subject: understanding 2PL parameterization with pre-specified latent variable scale
parts:
Hello Phil,

I've been exploring the use of mirt() for estimating 1PL and 2PL models in which the mean and variance of the ability distribution is specified in advance, and not equal to (0,1).  I am having trouble figuring out how to map the estimated parameters to the traditional 2PL parameterization. Script is below (I couldn't seem to attach)  I would appreciate any pointers as to how to do the transformation.  Thank you in advance and I appreciate your great software project.

best,
J.R.


## figuring out how to map mirt() 2PL item parameters to traditional IRT

## parameters when the latent variable distribution is set to a given mean and

## variance

set.seed(2321)

options(width=120)

library(mirt)


N       <- 200000

J       <- 10

mu      <- 5

sigmasq <- 2^2

theta   <- rnorm(N, mean=mu, sd=sqrt(sigmasq))


## J items with difficulties across ability range, and equal discriminations

a <- rep(1 / sqrt(sigmasq), J)

b <- seq(from = mu - 2*sqrt(sigmasq), to = mu + 2*sqrt(sigmasq), length=J)

X <- t(sapply(theta, function(x){ as.integer(runif(J) < (1 / (1 + exp(-a*(x - b))))) }))

colnames(X) <- paste0("it",1:J)

print(cbind(a=a,b=b))

print(apply(X, 2, mean))


p  <- mirt(X, 1, itemtype="2PL", pars="values")

## fix ability mean and variance at known population values

wh  <- which(p$name %in% c("MEAN_1","COV_11"))

p$est[wh]   <- FALSE

p$value[wh] <- c(mu, sigmasq)

print(p)

m1 <- mirt(X, 1, itemtype="2PL", pars=p)

print(coef(m1))

## print(tmp <- do.call("rbind",tmp[grep("it", names(tmp))]))

messages.subject: Re: understanding 2PL parameterization with pre-specified latent variable scale
parts: I solved the problem.  The issue is inconsistency between the integration grid used in the EM algorithm and my assumed prior distribution.  If I adjust the theta_lim to more sensible values, I recover the data generating parameters (code below).  This is in a weird space between user error and a bug.  I should have been more responsible about the integration grid.  On the other hand it might be good to print a warning message if the user specified a mean and variance for latent ability that has a lot of mass outside of the default integration region.

## figuring out how to map mirt() 2PL item parameters to traditional IRT

## parameters when the latent variable distribution is set to a given mean and

## variance

set.seed(2322)

options(width=120)

library(mirt)


N       <- 500000

J       <- 10

mu      <- 5

sigmasq <- 2^2

theta   <- rnorm(N, mean=mu, sd=sqrt(sigmasq))


## J items with difficulties across ability range, and equal discriminations

a <- rep(1 / sqrt(sigmasq), J)

b <- seq(from = mu - 2*sqrt(sigmasq), to = mu + 2*sqrt(sigmasq), length=J)

X <- t(sapply(theta, function(x){ as.integer(runif(J) < (1 / (1 + exp(-a*(x - b))))) }))

colnames(X) <- paste0("it",1:J)

print(cbind(a=a,b=b))

print(apply(X, 2, mean))


p  <- mirt(X, 1, itemtype="2PL", pars="values")

## fix ability mean and variance at known population values

wh  <- which(p$name %in% c("MEAN_1","COV_11"))

p$est[wh]   <- FALSE

p$value[wh] <- c(mu, sigmasq)

print(p)

m1 <- mirt(X, 1, itemtype="2PL", pars=p)


print(coef(m1))

## bad parameter estimates.  The issue is that the default theta_lim of (-6,6)

## does not sufficiently cover the range of theta under the specified N(5, 2^2)

## ability distribution

print(m1@Options$theta_lim)


## run with more sensible grid:

m2 <- mirt(X, 1, itemtype="2PL", pars=p, technical=list(theta_lim = c(-2,12)))

print(tmp <- coef(m2))

tmp <- do.call("rbind",tmp[grep("it", names(tmp))])[,c("a1","d")]


print(cbind(truth = a, est = tmp[,"a1"]))

print(cbind(truth = b, est = -tmp[,"d"]/tmp[,"a1"]))
